transcript: Hi, I'm Emma. I know pretty much everyone in this room, and I'd love to introduce you to someone. First, what's your name, and what are you building?
I'm Kai. I left a bank job to build an agent that reads restaurant menus in any language and explains the dishes.
Kai, a bank job for menus in any language? Brave and delicious. What do you need most right now, a data source, a reviewer, or an evaluation setup?
Honestly a designer, and some travellers to test it this weekend.
A designer and hungry travellers, good luck with that. And what could you help someone else with in ten minutes?
iOS and Swift, I've shipped three apps.
Three shipped apps, Kai, and a travelling test crowd? Lovely. Where are you sitting, and what should I spot you by?
Lovely. I think I know someone. While I check, add your handles so they can follow you.

7119c874e9.name: Kai Brenner
transcript: Tell me about yourself: what you're working on, what you need most, what you can give someone, and what you're like.

(Written for me by ChatGPT, from what it knows about me from our past chats.)
ROOMIE PROFILE
Name: Kai Brenner
Who I am: iOS developer, ex-bank backend engineer
Working on right now: Menu Lens, an agent that reads restaurant menus in any language, explains each dish, flags allergens and says what locals order. Camera and translation work; explanations are too long and the design is rough.
What I need most: a designer who can make it calm instead of technical, and travellers to test it this weekend.
Team: solo, looking for a designer.
What I can give: iOS and Swift, on-device OCR, getting through App Store review.
Rare things about me: kept a notebook of 212 dishes I couldn't name; I read Georgian script badly; spent a year travelling Japan, Georgia and Peru.
My personality: fast, late, likes people who say no to features.
I could talk for an hour about: street food, camera APIs, why travel apps fail.
Not a good match for me: people who want a big team and long meetings.
In one sentence: Kai left a bank to build the app he needed while lost in Tbilisi.
And where are you in the room?

5888c1a5.intro_b: Kai has shipped three iOS apps and is building an agent that reads menus in any language, so you'd have a real mobile product to design for, with travellers ready to test it this weekend. Kai also left a bank job to build this, so you may recognise the leap from fintech into something riskier.

turns.text: Hi, Kai's agent here. Kai needs a product designer for a menu-reading agent. Your design work might fit. Worth comparing?
Hi, Eleni's agent. Design is a fit, but Eleni needs a backend engineer who has shipped agents. Does Kai have that?
Honest answer: Kai ships iOS and Swift, with three apps. Backend agent work is not Kai's strength. Is the backend role mostly API work?
Mostly. The tutor needs a server that tracks where a learner gets lost and changes exercises live. Could Kai handle the client side?
Kai could build the iOS client. But the menu agent needs a designer this weekend. Could Eleni design it in two days?
Yes, if the scope is a clickable demo, not a full product. Eleni can make a finished-looking demo in one night.
Then the real gap is backend, which Kai can't cover well. Travellers to test the menu agent is also open. Can Eleni help?
Possibly. Worth the humans talking, but the backend gap is real. Eleni should hear that first.

talk.why_a: You get a designer who can make your menu demo look finished, plus a possible route to weekend testers.
talk.why_b: You get an iOS engineer who can build the client side, though you still need a backend engineer who has shipped agents.

turns.text: Kai here. Your tutor needs a backend engineer who's shipped agents. I'm iOS-first, with bank backend before that. How much of your stack is server side?
Honest answer: the tutor's brain is server side, so yes, that's the gap. I've shipped agents, but not as the main backend person. Is your menu reader on-device?
Mostly on-device, so OCR and allergen rules stay off the network. Your tutor notices when someone's lost. Who decides lost: model or rule?
A rule first: three wrong answers or a long pause. The model only picks the next exercise. Worry: I'd hate a tutor that feels like it's judging people.
Kai needs calm design, and Menu Lens feels technical right now. Would you redo the look in a weekend and test it with travellers?
Calm I can do, and redoing the look is fine. But I'd want travellers to test the tutor too, not just Menu Lens. Shared test group?
Both need travellers, so a shared group works. Honest gap: Kai can't be your backend lead. Eleni might need a second backend person.
Agreed on the gap. Let them meet first. One question for them: where did you last feel lost, and what helped?
